mainTopic: Testing רבה's principle of הואיל against plowing on יום טוב and against kindling in the five מלקות case, and whether מוקצה is a Torah prohibition.
overview: The גמרא is testing רבה's principle of הואיל: an act on יום טוב is not punished if it could have served a permitted יום טוב need. First it quotes a ברייתא that counts plowing on יום טוב as punishable, even though the loosened dirt could be used for כיסוי הדם. The גמרא tries several kinds of ground: hard clods, then rock-hard צונמא, then rock above loose soil. Each answer is knocked down. מר בר רב אשי finally answers that the ground was moist earth (מתונתא), which can be planted but cannot cover blood. Next אביי brings a ברייתא that gives five sets of מלקות for cooking גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב, one of them for kindling. רבה first replaces kindling with נבילה, but רבי חייא's count rules that out. So he replaces it with using עצי מוקצה, and he argues that מוקצה is a Torah prohibition. אביי then challenges רבה from רבה's own earlier question about a meadow lamb used for the תמיד, quoting a word-by-word דרשה on a verse in יחזקאל that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The end of the list of eight prohibitions in one furrow
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's list of eight לאוין for one furrow ends with שביעית, יום טוב, כהן, and נזיר plowing in a בית הטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...and it is the Sabbatical year, on a Festival, and the plower is a priest and a nazirite, plowing over a place of ritual impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a ברייתא that lists eight separate prohibitions a person can violate with one furrow. This quote is setup for the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier items (said on the previous עמוד) are plowing with an ox and a donkey together, both animals being הקדש, and כלאים בכרם. Here the list adds four more: שביעית, יום טוב, being a כהן, and being a נזיר who becomes טמא by walking over a grave area. The item that matters next is יום טוב, since the ברייתא counts plowing on יום טוב as a punishable prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh (Sabbatical) year, when working the land is forbidden
A Festival day, when מלאכה is forbidden except for food needs
A person under a vow who may not become impure from a dead body
A place made impure by a corpse or grave (בית הפרס)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement starting here. It is the end of a quote that began on the previous עמוד. The full list has eight items, not just these four.

phrases.english: and it is the Sabbatical year, on a Festival,
phrases.notes: The list keeps going. Before this came an ox and donkey together (כלאים), both of them consecrated, and כלאים in a vineyard.

phrases.english: a priest and a nazirite, over a place of impurity.
phrases.notes: Walking behind the plow over a grave area makes him impure, which is forbidden to both a כהן and a נזיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁבִיעִית, בְּיוֹם טוֹב, כֹּהֵן וְנָזִיר אַבֵּית הַטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא being cited against רבה's הואיל principle (cited on the previous עמוד).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One furrow can bring eight לאוין, including plowing on יום טוב.

steps.title: If we say הואיל, plowing on יום טוב should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: Under הואיל, plowing on יום טוב should not be punishable, because the loosened dirt could be used to cover the blood of a slaughtered bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we say "since" (הואיל), he should not be liable for plowing, since the dirt is fit for covering the blood of a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא to attack the principle of הואיל. If הואיל is correct, the ברייתא should not count plowing on יום טוב as a punishable act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, preparing something needed for that day, such as dirt for כיסוי הדם after a שחיטה, is allowed. By the logic of הואיל, the plowing could produce usable loose dirt, so it should not count as a forbidden מלאכה. Yet the ברייתא does count it, which seems to disprove הואיל.

keyTerms.meaning: "Since": an act counts as permitted because it could potentially serve a permitted purpose
Plowing
The מצוה to cover the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal with dirt
Is fit or suitable

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a direct test of רבה's principle. If no answer is found, הואיל would be disproven.

phrases.english: And if we say the principle of "since"
phrases.notes: Refers to רבה's principle.

phrases.english: he should not be liable for the plowing,
phrases.notes: He means liable for breaking יום טוב.

phrases.english: since it is fit for covering the blood of a bird.
phrases.notes: The loosened earth could be used for כיסוי הדם on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted as ammunition against הואיל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes plowing on יום טוב punishable. But under הואיל it should be exempt, since the dirt could serve כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: The plowing was through hard clods
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא בר שמואל answers that the ground was made of hard clods of earth, which cannot be used to cover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא בר שמואל said: It is a case of hardened clods (sharp stones).
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא בר שמואל defends הואיל by changing the case. The ground in the ברייתא was hard clods, not loose dirt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הואיל only works if the result is actually fit for a יום טוב use. Hard clods are not fit for covering blood, so הואיל does not apply, and the plowing stays punishable. The ברייתא no longer contradicts הואיל.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharp, hardened clods of earth

phrases.english: Rav Pappa bar Shmuel said:
With hardened, sharp clods.
phrases.notes: This earth is unfit for covering blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: בַּאֲבָנִים מְקוּרְזָלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about ordinary soil, which is fit for כיסוי הדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about hard clods, which are unfit, so הואיל does not apply.

steps.title: The clods could be crushed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the clods are fit to be crushed into dust, so they are still potentially usable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are fit to be crushed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. The hard clods could be crushed into dust, so they are still potentially fit for covering blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הואיל works on potential usefulness. Since the clods can become dust, the potential for כיסוי הדם seems to remain, and the problem returns.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushing or pounding
Fit or suitable

phrases.english: They are fit to be crushed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא בר שמואל's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Clods can be crushed into usable dirt, so they are still potentially fit for כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: Crushing on יום טוב is itself forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that crushing is not permitted on יום טוב, so the clods cannot become usable dirt today.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is crushing permitted on a Festival?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the answer with a rhetorical question. Crushing is itself forbidden on יום טוב, so the clods cannot legally be made fit today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A potential use only counts if it can be done legally on יום טוב. Since crushing is forbidden, the clods are not truly fit, and the answer of אבנים מקורזלות stands.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is it permitted?" (rhetorical: no, it is not)

steps.confusionAlert: This is phrased as a question, but it functions as an answer: "Of course crushing is not allowed!"

phrases.english: And is crushing on a Festival permitted?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection that the clods could be crushed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Legal limitation on the potential use
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The possibility of crushing makes the clods fit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Crushing is forbidden on יום טוב, so it does not create fitness.

steps.title: They could be crushed in an unusual way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא counters that the clods could be crushed כלאחר יד (in an unusual manner), which is not a Torah prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are fit to be crushed in an unusual manner!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. Crushing done in an unusual way (כלאחר יד) is not a Torah-level מלאכה, so the clods are still potentially usable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An act done כלאחר יד is not forbidden on a Torah level. So the clods can be made usable without a Torah violation, and the challenge against הואיל returns.

keyTerms.meaning: In an unusual, back-handed manner (not a Torah-level מלאכה)

phrases.english: They are fit to be crushed in an unusual manner!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense that crushing is forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that crushing is forbidden on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Crushing כלאחר יד is not a Torah prohibition, so the clods are still potentially fit.

steps.title: The ground was rock-hard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is צונמא, rock-hard ground that cannot be crushed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: With hard, rocky soil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The plowing was in צונמא, ground so hard it cannot be crushed in any way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ground cannot be crushed at all, there is no possible way to make it fit for כיסוי הדם. So הואיל has nothing to work with, and the plowing stays punishable.

keyTerms.meaning: Hard, rocky ground

phrases.english: With hard, rocky ground.
phrases.notes: A single word, but it is a complete answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the clod answer with a harder type of ground.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ground was clods, which could be crushed כלאחר יד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ground was צונמא, which can never become usable dirt.

steps.title: Rock-hard ground cannot be planted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether צונמא is fit for planting at all. The ברייתא assumes real agricultural plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is hard rocky ground fit for planting?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the צונמא answer. The ברייתא counts כלאים and שביעית, which only make sense for plowing land meant for growing, and rock cannot be planted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's other prohibitions assume this is real farming plowing. Plowing pure rock is not agricultural work, so the ברייתא could not be talking about צונמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for planting

phrases.english: Is hard rocky ground fit for planting?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the צונמא answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא assumes plantable land (כלאים, שביעית), but צונמא cannot be planted.

steps.title: Hard layer on top, loose soil underneath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there was צונמא on top and loose, plantable soil (עפר תיחוח) below.
steps.simpleTranslation: Hard ground above, and loose soil below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refines the case. The top layer was rock-hard, and underneath was loose soil where seeds could grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tries to satisfy both needs at once. The loose soil underneath makes it farmland, so כלאים and שביעית apply. The hard top layer is supposed to explain why the plowing does not produce usable dirt.

keyTerms.meaning: Soft, loose soil
From above / from below

phrases.english: Hard ground above,
and loose soil below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection that צונמא cannot be planted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole field is rock, so it is not farmland.
steps.terutzMaskana: Rock is on top and loose soil is below, so it is farmland.

steps.title: The loose soil underneath should make it exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the loose soil underneath is fit for covering blood, so הואיל should exempt the plowing after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But derive the exemption because of the loose soil!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. If there is loose soil underneath, that soil is fit for כיסוי הדם, so הואיל should still apply and exempt the plowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer that made the field plantable also brought back usable dirt. Adding loose soil underneath undoes the reason הואיל was supposed to fail, so the original challenge returns.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let him derive it" from another reason

steps.whatToRemember: Each answer tries to make the ground unusable for כיסוי הדם (so הואיל fails) while keeping it plantable (so the ברייתא's other prohibitions make sense). The צונמא approach cannot do both. Steps 11-13 solve the problem with a new kind of ground.

phrases.english: But derive it [an exemption] because of the loose soil!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the refined case by showing it brings back the original problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of צונמא above and loose soil below
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The loose soil underneath is fit for כיסוי הדם, so by הואיל the plowing should be exempt, and the ברייתא still contradicts הואיל.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי: the case is plowing mud
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי answers the last קשיא. The case is plowing טינא (mud), and mud cannot be used to cover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said: the case is one where he plowed mud.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the צונמא answer and gives a new one. The person plowed mud, which can never be used to cover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last קשיא said that loose soil is fit for כיסוי הדם, so הואיל should exempt the plowing. Blood must be covered with dry, crumbly dust, and wet mud does not work for that. So there is no הואיל here, and the plowing is a real Torah violation.

keyTerms.meaning: Mud; wet, sticky earth
Rather; this word drops the earlier answer and starts a new one
The מצוה of covering the blood of a slaughtered bird or wild animal with dust

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
phrases.notes: אלא tells us the צונמא answer is being given up.

phrases.english: It is a case of mud.
phrases.notes: Mud cannot be used to cover blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by replacing the soil type with one that cannot cover blood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any plowed earth could be used for covering blood, so הואיל would always exempt the plowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Mud cannot cover blood, so plowing it is not exempted by הואיל.

steps.title: Is mud even plantable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether mud can be planted at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is mud fit for planting?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. Can anyone actually plant in mud?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is talking about real farm plowing, which is done to prepare ground for planting. If mud cannot be planted, plowing it is not true plowing. Then the case no longer fits the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit for planting

phrases.english: And is mud fit for planting?!
phrases.notes: He isn't really asking. He means you can't normally plant in mud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the mud answer of step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the case is plowing mud
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Plowing only counts as plowing if the ground can be planted, and mud cannot be planted.

steps.title: Moist earth: plantable but cannot cover blood
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the case is מתונתא, damp earth. It can be planted but cannot be used to cover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case of moist earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the answer. The ground was not soupy mud but damp earth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damp earth works for planting, so plowing it is real plowing. It is still too wet to count as dust for כיסוי הדם. Both conditions are now met, so there is no הואיל, and the plowing on יום טוב is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Moist, damp earth; plantable but too wet to cover blood

steps.whatToRemember: The plowing case is resolved this way: the ground is moist earth, good for planting but not usable for covering blood. So הואיל does not apply.

phrases.english: In moist earth.
phrases.notes: Damp soil, between mud and dry dust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by refining 'mud' into 'moist earth'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mud cannot be planted, so the case falls apart.
steps.terutzMaskana: Moist earth can be planted but cannot cover blood. Plowing it is liable even if we accept הואיל.

steps.title: אביי cites the five lashes for cooking גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. Someone who cooks גיד הנשה in milk on יום טוב and eats it gets five sets of מלקות, and one of them is for הבערה (kindling).
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged him: One who cooks the sciatic nerve in milk on יום טוב and eats it is lashed five times. He is lashed for cooking the nerve on יום טוב, for eating the nerve, for cooking meat in milk, for eating meat in milk, and for kindling.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new source to challenge רבה's principle of הואיל. This step only sets up the source; the actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cooking on יום טוב is normally allowed for food. גיד הנשה is forbidden, so cooking it is not for food, and that makes it liable. The key item is the fifth one, kindling a fire for no real need. That is the item אביי will attack.

keyTerms.meaning: The sciatic nerve, which the Torah forbids eating
He receives מלקות (lashes)
Kindling a fire
Meat with milk; forbidden to cook and to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Cooking on יום טוב is usually permitted for food. Here it is liable only because the item being cooked, גיד הנשה, is forbidden and not real food.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
phrases.notes: Aimed at רבה, who holds הואיל.

phrases.english: One who cooks the sciatic nerve in milk
on a Festival and eats it is lashed five times.

phrases.aramaic: לוֹקֶה מִשּׁוּם מְבַשֵּׁל גִּיד בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: He is lashed for cooking the nerve on a Festival,
phrases.notes: It is not food, so it is not permitted cooking.

phrases.english: and he is lashed for eating the nerve,
and he is lashed for cooking meat in milk,
and he is lashed for eating meat in milk,
and he is lashed for kindling.
phrases.notes: This is the item אביי will challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רבה's principle of הואיל, using a different case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the ברייתא counts kindling as a punishable act.

steps.title: אביי: הואיל should exempt the kindling
steps.stepSummary: If we accept הואיל, the kindling should not be punished, because that same fire could have been used for a permitted need.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we say 'since', he should not be liable for kindling, since the fire is fit for his needs!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the punchline of אביי's challenge. Under הואיל, the kindling should not count, but the ברייתא does count it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire he lit could have been used to cook permitted food for יום טוב. By הואיל, a potential permitted use should take away liability. The ברייתא still punishes the kindling, which suggests it rejects הואיל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': because the act could have served a permitted purpose, there is no liability
For his (permitted) needs

phrases.english: And if we say 'since',
he should not be liable for the kindling,
since it is fit for his needs!
phrases.notes: The fire could cook permitted food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection set up in step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא punishes kindling even though הואיל would exempt it, so the ברייתא seems to reject הואיל.

steps.title: רבה: swap kindling for eating נבילה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers by fixing the list. Take out הבערה and add a different item: the גיד came from a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Remove kindling, and insert the sciatic nerve of a נבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה keeps the total of five but changes what the five are. The case is a גיד from an animal that died without proper שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With kindling removed, the ברייתא no longer goes against הואיל. To keep the count at five, eating נבילה becomes the fifth prohibition. רבה reads the ברייתא as a different case instead of giving up his principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Take out
Put in
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; forbidden to eat

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבה answering אביי.

phrases.english: Remove kindling,
and insert the sciatic nerve of a carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 by changing the items in the ברייתא's list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the text and case of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Kindling is one of the five, which goes against הואיל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Kindling is not counted. The fifth item is eating נבילה, so הואיל stands.

steps.title: רבי חייא counts three for cooking, not three for eating
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא taught two lashes for eating and three for cooking. Under רבה's version there should be three for eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי חייא taught: they are lashed twice for eating it and three times for cooking it. And if it is as you say, he should have said three for eating it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבה's change by quoting רבי חייא's breakdown of the five lashes. The count in that breakdown does not match רבה's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three for cooking means cooking on יום טוב, cooking meat with milk, and kindling. So kindling is in the list. If the fifth item were נבילה, eating would carry three lashes (the גיד, meat with milk, and נבילה). רבי חייא says two, so רבה's version does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (in a ברייתא)
And if it were so
He should have said

steps.confusionAlert: Count which actions are cooking and which are eating. The challenge depends entirely on the 2 versus 3 split.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya teach:
They are lashed twice for eating it,
phrases.notes: Eating the גיד and eating meat with milk.

phrases.english: and three for cooking it.
phrases.notes: Cooking on יום טוב, cooking meat with milk, and kindling.

phrases.english: And if it is so (as you say),
he should have said three for eating it!
phrases.notes: Because נבילה would be a third eating prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's change in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's swap of kindling for נבילה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's split (two for eating, three for cooking) only works if kindling is counted and נבילה is not.

steps.title: Remove kindling and add set-aside wood instead
steps.stepSummary: רבה gives a new fix. He takes הבערה out of the list and puts in using עצי מוקצה. This keeps eating at two lashes and cooking at three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: take out 'kindling,' and put in 'set-aside wood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה drops his earlier fix, which added נבילה, because it gave three lashes for eating. He gives a new fix that matches רבי חייא's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under הואיל, kindling the fire cannot be punished, so הבערה still has to leave the list. The replacement now goes on the cooking side: the person cooked with wood that was מוקצה. Eating stays at two lashes and cooking stays at three, just as רבי חייא taught.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier answer and offers a new one.
Take out, remove
Put in, add
Wood that was set aside and not prepared for use before יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: This fix does not bring back the נבילה answer. The word אלא means רבה is replacing that answer with a new one.

phrases.english: Rather:
remove 'kindling,'
and insert 'set-aside wood.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אַפֵּיק הַבְעָרָה, וְעַיֵּיל עֲצֵי מוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17's count problem by changing which item replaces הבערה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: the list in the ברייתא is changed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The replacement item was נבילה, which raised the eating count to three.
steps.terutzMaskana: The replacement is עצי מוקצה on the cooking side, so the count stays two for eating and three for cooking.

steps.title: Is מוקצה really forbidden by the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether מוקצה is a Torah prohibition. מלקות are given only for Torah prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is מוקצה a Torah-level prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבה's new fix. Lashes are given only for breaking a Torah law, so is מוקצה Torah law?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many people assume מוקצה is a rabbinic rule. If it is rabbinic, it cannot be one of the five sets of lashes, and רבה's fix fails. The question looks like a simple inquiry, but it works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah, Torah-level
Lashes. They are given only for Torah prohibitions.

phrases.english: And is set-aside material prohibited by Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the item רבה added in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that עצי מוקצה earns מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lashes require a Torah prohibition. If מוקצה is only rabbinic, it cannot fill the empty spot in the list.

steps.title: Yes: a verse for the rule and a verse for the warning
steps.stepSummary: רבה says מוקצה is Torah law. The rule comes from 'והכינו את אשר יביאו.' The אזהרה comes from 'לא תעשה כל מלאכה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, as it is written: 'And it shall be on the sixth day that they shall prepare what they bring.' And its warning comes from here: 'You shall not do any work.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that מוקצה is a Torah prohibition. He gives a verse for the rule and a second verse for the formal warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about preparing on the sixth day teaches that only food prepared ahead may be used. Lashes need a negative commandment, called an אזהרה, so רבה adds 'לא תעשה כל מלאכה' as the warning. With both verses, using מוקצה wood can earn מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall prepare. This is the source that things must be prepared in advance.
A formal negative warning, which is needed before מלקות can be given
You shall not do any work

steps.whyThisMatters: The source for the rule and the source for the punishment are separate pieces. A verse that shows something is forbidden is not enough for מלקות without a לאו.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
as it is written: 'And it shall be on the sixth day
that they shall prepare what they bring in.'
And its warning is from here:
from 'You shall not do any work.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 19 by giving Torah sources.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מוקצה might be only rabbinic, so it could not earn lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: מוקצה is Torah law, with a verse for the rule and a לאו as its אזהרה, so it can earn מלקות.

steps.title: אביי recalls רבה's question about a meadow lamb used as the daily offering
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with רבה's own earlier report. רבה had asked רב חסדא, or by another version רב הונא, whether a lamb brought from the meadow may be slaughtered as the תמיד on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But weren't you the one who said: 'I asked רב חסדא (some say: I asked רב הונא): If one brought a lamb from the meadow and slaughtered it as the daily offering on יום טוב, what is the law?'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a challenge against רבה. He reminds רבה of a question about a מוקצה lamb that רבה himself once asked his teacher. This line sets up the challenge, and the punch comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lamb out grazing in the meadow was not prepared before יום טוב, so it is מוקצה. רבה had treated its use for the תמיד as an open question. אביי is about to show that the answer רבה received does not fit a view that מוקצה is clear Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: But weren't you the one who said. It challenges someone from his own words.
I asked him, I raised a question before him
A lamb from the meadow. It was not prepared beforehand, so it is מוקצה.
The daily communal offering

phrases.english: He said to him:
But weren't you the one who said:
I asked Rav Chisda,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: בְּעַאי מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: and some say: I asked Rav Huna:
If one brought a lamb from the meadow,
and slaughtered it as the daily offering on a Festival, what is the law?

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: שאלה (the quoted inquiry inside the challenge)
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, וְהָא אַתְּ הוּא דַּאֲמַרְתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts attacking Step 20's claim that מוקצה is Torah law, using רבה's own past statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim in Step 20 that מוקצה is a Torah prohibition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה's own earlier exchange about a מוקצה lamb, and the answer he reported, suggest that מוקצה was not treated as clear Torah law.

steps.title: The answer רבה reported: a lamb, but not a firstborn
steps.stepSummary: אביי continues quoting רבה. The answer רבה received was a דרשה on a verse in יחזקאל: 'שה,' but not a בכור. The challenge continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you told us that he told me about it: 'A lamb,' and not a firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins quoting the answer רבה received, which was a דרשה on a verse in יחזקאל about communal offerings. The דרשה goes through the verse word by word. It continues in steps 23-24 and onto the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teacher answered from a verse in יחזקאל, expounding each word to exclude certain animals. 'שה' excludes a בכור. This exclusion is not itself about מוקצה. It is the first item in a list, and the part that bears on the meadow lamb comes later in the verse, on the next עמוד. That is where אביי builds his challenge against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: And you told us
About it, on this matter
A firstborn animal, which has its own holiness

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a final ruling of the סוגיא. It is the inner answer quoted inside אביי's challenge, and the challenge is completed on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: And you told us,
(he said to me) about it:
'A lamb,' and not a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted exchange begun in Step 21 by giving the answer the teacher gave.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a meadow lamb, which is מוקצה, may be offered as the תמיד on יום טוב
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The teacher answered with a word-by-word דרשה on the verse in יחזקאל, beginning with 'שה': a lamb, but not a בכור. The clause that addresses the meadow lamb comes later in the דרשה, on the next עמוד.

steps.title: The word 'one' excludes a tithe animal
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה continues. The word 'אחת' in the verse teaches that a מעשר בהמה may not be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'one.' This means not an animal from the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is still quoting the answer רבה received. The next word of the יחזקאל verse, 'אחת', rules out a מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of the verse is read as cutting out one kind of animal. 'One' suggests an animal that stands alone. A מעשר בהמה is always part of a group, because it is the tenth animal counted out of the pen, so it cannot serve as this offering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One': read as an animal that stands on its own
Animal tithe: every tenth animal counted out of the pen is holy

phrases.english: 'One': and not a tithe animal.
phrases.notes: The tithe animal only becomes holy as the tenth of a group. It is never a 'single' animal.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is still part of the answer אביי is quoting from רבה's own report, which began in Step 22.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the word-by-word דרשה begun in Step 22 ("שה" but not a בכור).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which animals are fit to be brought as the communal offering described in יחזקאל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'אחת' excludes a מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: 'From the flock' excludes an in-between animal
steps.stepSummary: The words 'מן הצאן' teach that a פלגס may not be brought. A פלגס is an animal past the age of a lamb but not yet a ram.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'from the flock.' This means not a פלגס.
steps.whatsHappening: The דרשה goes on to the next words, 'מן הצאן'. These words rule out a פלגס. The list of דרשות keeps going on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מן' means 'from' or 'some of.' It is read as limiting: only some animals of the flock qualify. A פלגס is in an in-between age. It no longer counts as a lamb and is not yet a ram, so it is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From the flock': the word 'from' limits which animals qualify
An animal in between: too old to be a lamb, too young to be a ram

phrases.english: 'From the flock': and not a palges.
phrases.notes: פלגס falls between the category of כבש (lamb) and the category of איל (ram).

steps.whyThisMatters: These דרשות show that the verse is read very closely, word by word. אביי will use one of these דרשות to challenge רבה's claim that מוקצה is a Torah prohibition.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the next exclusion in the same derasha.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which animals are fit to be brought as the communal offering described in יחזקאל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'מן הצאן' exclude a פלגס.
